Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

zumime 0.0.0.9000

  • Initial CRAN submission.
  • zumime_info() reports the package version and the version of the type tables.
  • A type registry generated from IANA’s media types registry and Apache httpd’s mime.types, with parents ending at application/octet-stream and aliases. mime_types() returns it; zumime_info()$table_version is the date of its sources.
  • mime_guess() guesses a type from a file name, knowing compound suffixes such as .tar.gz; mime_extensions() is the reverse.
  • mime_parent() gives a type’s lineage and mime_is() tests whether a type is, or descends from, a type, an alias or a top-level type.
  • mime_parse() and mime_format() parse and serialise a MIME type as the WHATWG MIME Sniffing Standard defines it.
  • mime_sniff() runs the WHATWG MIME Sniffing Standard’s algorithm over a raw vector, with a supplied type, the no-sniff flag and a sniffing context, and reports the charset the bytes declare and their line endings. Beyond the standard it knows the compression wrappers, tar, ISO 9660 images, RAR 5, 7z, fonts and WebAssembly.
  • In the default "none" context mime_sniff() reads containers: ZIP entry names tell Office Open XML (with its macro-enabled, template and slideshow variants), OpenDocument, EPUB, JAR, APK and 3MF documents from plain ZIP; OLE2 directories tell Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook and installer files; ISO base media brands tell MP4, M4A, M4V, QuickTime, 3GP, HEIC, HEIF, AVIF and CR3 apart; EBML and Ogg headers name their codecs.
  • R’s own files are recognised through gzip: RDS and RData, as are Parquet, Arrow and Feather, fst, qs2, SQLite, DuckDB, HDF5, NetCDF, Stata, SPSS and SAS files.
  • Structured text is typed at "probable": XML dialects by root element and namespace, JSON and its dialects by top-level keys, NDJSON, and line-oriented formats such as vCard, iCalendar, WebVTT and PEM.
  • encrypted reports ZIP entries encrypted with the classic flag or AES, and OLE2 files holding an EncryptionInfo stream; interpreter names a script’s shebang program.
  • text/xml is now an alias of application/xml.
  • mime_type() types files from their bytes and their names in one C loop, says whether the two agree, and reports what a consumer needs to open each file: the type inside a compression wrapper (inner), whether it is encrypted, whether it is complete (complete = TRUE reads the end of ZIP, PDF, gzip and Parquet files), its line endings and a script’s interpreter. Unreadable paths are NA rows unless strict = TRUE.
  • mime_sniff() also takes paths.
  • mime_check() answers whether files are one of a set of allowed types from their bytes alone, faster than mime_type() and always with the same answer.
  • mime_register() and mime_unregister() add a type for the session, detected by a byte rule in C or by an R function.
  • Optional help from the family, never consulted unless asked: inner = "decompress" (zukomp), text = "family" (zucsv, zujson, zutoml) and charset = "detect" (zuutf). zumime_info()$family lists the family sniffers available.
  • mime_sniffer(), mime_push() and mime_finish() sniff a stream chunk by chunk and answer as soon as the bytes seen decide the type.

Developed by Pedro Baltazar.
